raw_response:
I've farmed this land for 15 years. I know what works here in Quzhou. The soil is decent, I have the well, and my family needs steady income. Some of my kids work in town, so I can't count on much extra labor from them during busy periods — I have to plan around that.

**My thinking:**

Cotton is my main money crop. I'll put most of my land — about 12 mu — into cotton. I've been using hybrid Bt cotton for several years now. Everyone around here does. It handles bollworm better and I don't need as many spray runs. I'll rotary till before planting in late April. I put down compound fertilizer as base and top-dress with urea during the boll-setting stage. I irrigate from the well — usually 4 times: before planting, at seedling, at boll formation, and once more at late boll stage. I still spray 6 times over the season — aphids and spider mites come every year no matter what.

For the remaining nearly 5 mu, I grow summer maize. I plant it separately in early June. Maize doesn't need as much attention as cotton. Hybrid seed, rotary till, 3 irrigations, a couple of pest sprays. It gives me grain for the family and some to sell.

I don't try new things I haven't seen work locally. I follow what the village extension station and my neighbors use. It's not perfect but I know the risks.
